To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the structure of the primary, hydroxy and ferryl intermediates of O2 reduction by cytochrome c oxidoase.

“the first step of dioxygen (O2) reduction by reduced cytochrome oxidase (cyt c ox) involves a ferryl–peroxide (Fe4+=OOH) intermediate and the subsequent 4-electron reaction is initiated by the formation of a ferric-hydrate (Fe3+OH2) intermediate.”

the primary, ferric–oxo (ferryl) and ferric–hydroxy intermediates in O2 reduction by cytochrome c oxidoase are identified by their iron–oxygen stretching frequencies (785, 450 and 520cm−1, respectively) and oxygen and deuteration isotope shifts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalytic mechanism of cytochrome c Oxidase (CcO), which is a key enzyme of cellular energy transduction.
the mechanism of dioxygen activation in cytochrome c Oxidase.
the structure and function of the heme proteins of the respiratory chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the O2 reduction proceeds via a ferryl intermediate, and that the hydroxy intermediate, formed by the addition of water to this intermediate, is a key intermediate in the catalytic cycle, and not an intermediate in a side reaction.

the reaction of O(2) with the reduced cytochrome oxidase is initiated by the binding of O(2), which is then reduced by two electrons to a peroxo (Fe(4+)-O(2)2−) intermediate, which is subsequently reduced by two electrons and protonated to form the ferryl intermediate (Fe(4+)O(2)−), which then undergoes two further protonation steps to form water and a hydroxy intermediate (Fe(3

the O2 molecule is reduced to water by four successive 2-electron transfers, with the first electron transferred to dioxygen to give the ferryl intermediate, the second electron transferred to the ferryl group to yield the ferric-hydroperoxo intermediate, the third electron transferred to the peroxo group to give the hydroxy intermediate, and the fourth electron to yield the water molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cytochrome c oxidation is the primary reaction of O2 reduction, and that the ferryl and hydroxyl intermediates are formed by protonation of O2 and H2O, respectively, in a concerted reaction with O-O bond cleavage.
the catalytic intermediacy of the primary intermediate is confirmed, and the ferryl and hydroxyl intermediates are identified and characterized.

the O2 reduction is initiated by a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanism, which involves a hydrogen-bonded Fe4+=O− intermediate and is followed by an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) reaction, which produces a Fe4+=O intermediate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the iron–oxygens in the catalytic intermediacy of cytochrome c-oxidase (CcO) are all very weakly bonded and the O2 reduction proceeds by a series of proton-coupled electron transfer steps.
the reaction of dioxygen with the heme a3–CuB binuclear center in cytochrome c oxidaserequires the participation of a tyrosine residue, Tyr244, which is hydrogen bonded to a water molecule.
the reaction mechanism of the enzyme is very similar to that of the free heme proteins.
